about.title: Lake Forest Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a death in Lake Forest is caused by someone else's carelessness, the paperwork arrives long before the grief settles. The city recorded three traffic deaths in 2025, alongside 163 injury collisions that hurt 244 people. Behind each of those numbers is a household trying to work out what happens next. California gives certain family members the right to bring a wrongful death claim, a civil action that stands apart from any criminal case the district attorney may or may not pursue. Standing is limited: a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children come first, followed by specific dependents and heirs. The claim can seek funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the person would have provided, and the harder-to-measure loss of their love, companionship and guidance. Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shrinks considerably when a public agency is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect Lake Forest families, at no charge, with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency.

items.title: The two-year clock, explained
items.desc: Most claims must be brought within two years of the date of death, and the deadline is far shorter when a city, county or state agency is involved. Early guidance keeps that window open.

items.title: Separate from the criminal case
items.desc: A wrongful death claim is a civil action, so it proceeds whether or not prosecutors bring charges. The attorneys we connect you with work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My spouse was killed in a crash on the I-5 through Lake Forest. Does a criminal investigation affect our claim?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim in California is a civil action that moves forward independently of anything the Orange County District Attorney decides. Evidence gathered by investigators may be useful, but your family does not have to wait for charges or a conviction. An independent attorney can help preserve records from the CHP or Orange County Sheriff's Department while they are still available.

items.question: What losses can our family recover in a California wrongful death case?
items.answer: Recoverable losses generally include funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have contributed over their expected lifetime, and the loss of their love, companionship, care and guidance. Each family's situation is different, so no one can predict a specific result. An attorney can walk through how these categories apply to your circumstances.

items.question: How long do we have to file after a death in Lake Forest?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. If a government entity might be responsible — for example, a city vehicle or a claim involving road maintenance on a public street like Lake Forest Drive — a formal claim must usually be presented within six months. Because these deadlines are strict, it is wise to speak with an attorney sooner rather than later.
